_notes: Overlay, not a standalone profile — merge onto a base with scripts/merge_style_profile.py, don't pass this file as --style on its own. Captures what actually changes for a <60s vertical Shorts/Reels/TikTok cut of the same channel style: tighter pacing, a compressed arc, mobile/sound-off-safe captions, and a UI safe zone. Everything not listed here (color, camera_motion vocabulary, sound_design layering, transitions.backbone) stays whatever the base profile says — a Shorts cut should still look like the same show, just edited for the format. This overlay does NOT set aspect ratio by itself — both profiles already define a '9:16' entry under aspect_ratios; remember to pass --aspect 9:16 explicitly to scripts/resolve/build_project.py (the only script that takes it) when building a Shorts cut, the same as any other project.

narrative_arc.notes: The full essay arc (thesis/example/proof/abstraction) doesn't fit in Shorts runtime — compress straight from hook to the strongest single payoff. If the source material has a long-form beat plan already, this is usually the escalation/climax section of that plan, re-cut standalone, not the whole story retold small.

composition.safe_zone: Keep primary subjects/text within the center ~80% of frame width and out of the bottom ~15%/right ~12% — platform UI (captions, like/comment/share, profile) typically sits there. Verify against the actual target platform before finalizing, this is a general guideline not a pixel spec for any one app.

captions.style_notes: Bigger relative to frame than the long-form default — mobile viewing, often at arm's length. Treat captions as load-bearing, not optional: a large share of Shorts-style viewing happens muted, so the caption track has to carry the video on its own, not just reinforce audio someone's already hearing.
